text:
tara: Heads up — quick sync on 'surgeflow' as a canary-surge handling layer + fallback cohesion. WDYT about adding a surge window and probe aggregation? cc @raj @linh

raj: Love it. Concern: when canary autos-scales because of a burst, we might flip routing before probes stabilise -> false positives and noisy rollbacks.

linh: Can we add a 'probe_stability' guard: require N consecutive probe passes across M windows, and make it configurable by p95 latency and error-rate thresholds?

michael: Also need version affinity for sticky sessions — otherwise KV cache churn destroys the perf signal for the canary.

jamie: What about short-lived 'grace_seats' — a temporary quota so the canary only absorbs X% of burst traffic while probes run. That keeps tail risk bounded. :thinking_face: 

raj: Sketch config I had in mind:
```yaml
surgeflow:
  window_ms: 5000
  probe_consecutive: 3
  probe_windows: 4
  p95_threshold_ms: 120
  error_rate_threshold_pct: 1.0
  grace_seats_pct: 10
  recovery_window_min_minutes: 10
```

tara: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we define the fallback chain? 2) what runtime interface does the router need to coordinate failover and telemetry?

linh: Fallback chain proposal: identical_variant -> quantized_variant -> regional_fallback -> degrade_path (e.g., cached response / shorter context). Each step emits a structured event with reason, metric snapshot, and a sanitized sample dump for offline repro.

michael: Router needs a tiny API surface for this: routeFallback(reason, target_variant, options) that is idempotent and returns a decision token. Also we need a sidecar hook for session_affinity: acquireAffinity(session_id, variant, ttl).

tara: Good. Also ensure sample dumps scrub PII at the edge before storage. We should capture only the minimal context needed for model-regression eval.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-4781 to add probe_stability and routeFallback API (assigned: jamie, michael).

jamie: :thumbsup: Add backoff slot too so repeated flaps don't oscillate — exponential backoff with jitter and a floor that triggers operator alert.

raj: Edge-case to watch: burst + network degradation -> probe timeouts -> fallback, then underlying infra recovers but canary remains out because probes still failing due to affinity/cache cold. Suggest a 'recovery_window' that permits re-evaluation with a tokenized slow ramp (token-slice) rather than full immediate reinclusion.

linh: Recovery sketch: token-slice ramp starting at 1% traffic for T minutes, doubling every successful window until target share reached. Each step requires probe stability check.

tara: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with concrete config schema and runtime contracts. Want to include a couple of test-cases: burst-with-cache-warmup, region-network-lag, and quantized-fallback-quality-check.

jamie: I can own the router changes and backoff logic.

michael: I'll own session affinity and the routeFallback mock + unit tests.

tara: Thanks — I'll put a draft in the doc bucket and schedule a sync next Wed. Draft link: https://redwood/internal/docs/surgeflow-canary (internal).

raj: One more note — let's add probes that run from both origin and edge egress points so we catch regional network issues vs model regressions.

tara: Good call. Closing this thread for now — follow-up in #eng-platform next Wed.
